questions.accessible_text:
1. [Maximum mark: 6]

The following diagram shows a circle with centre O and radius r.

[Diagram not to scale: points A and B lie on the circumference; OA and OB bound the shaded minor sector AOB, whose central angle is 1 radian.]

Points A and B lie on the circumference of the circle, and AÔB=1 radian. The perimeter of the shaded region is 12.

(a) Find the value of r. [3]

(b) Hence, find the exact area of the non-shaded region. [3]
questions.solution: (a) Arc AB=r, so perimeter r+r+r=3r=12 and r=4. (b) Non-shaded angle is 2π−1, so area=(1/2)(16)(2π−1)=16π−8.

questions.accessible_text:
2. [Maximum mark: 4]

Consider two consecutive positive integers, n and n+1. Show that the difference of their squares is equal to the sum of the two integers.
questions.solution: Subtract the smaller square from the larger: (n+1)²−n²=n²+2n+1−n²=2n+1. The sum is n+(n+1)=2n+1, so the two expressions are equal, as required.

questions.accessible_text:
3. [Maximum mark: 6]

(a) Show that the equation 2cos²x+5sinx=4 may be written in the form 2sin²x−5sinx+2=0. [1]

(b) Hence, solve the equation 2cos²x+5sinx=4, 0≤x≤2π. [5]
questions.solution: (a) Substitute cos²x=1−sin²x and rearrange. (b) (2sinx−1)(sinx−2)=0. Only sinx=1/2 is possible, so x=π/6,5π/6.

questions.accessible_text:
4. [Maximum mark: 5]

In the expansion of (x+k)⁷, where k∈ℝ, the coefficient of the term in x⁵ is 63. Find the possible values of k.
questions.solution: The x⁵ term is C(7,5)x⁵k²=21k²x⁵. Thus k²=3 and k=±√3.

questions.accessible_text:
5. [Maximum mark: 9]

Consider the function f defined by f(x)=ln(x²−16) for x>4. The following diagram shows part of the graph of f, which crosses the x-axis at point A, with coordinates (a,0). The line L is the tangent to the graph of f at the point B.

[Diagram: the graph has vertical asymptote x=4, crosses at A(a,0), and has tangent L at B.]

(a) Find the exact value of a. [3]

(b) Given that the gradient of L is 1/3, find the x-coordinate of B. [6]
questions.solution: (a) ln(a²−16)=0 gives a²=17; a>4, so a=√17. (b) f′=2x/(x²−16)=1/3 gives x²−6x−16=0, hence x=8 or −2. Domain leaves x=8.

questions.accessible_text:
6. [Maximum mark: 7]

The following diagram shows triangle ABC, with AB=10, BC=x and AC=2x.

[Diagram not to scale: triangle ABC with side lengths AB=10, BC=x and AC=2x.]

Given that cosC=3/4, find the area of the triangle in the form p√q/2, where p,q∈ℤ⁺. [7]
questions.solution: Cosine rule: 100=x²+4x²−4x²(3/4)=2x², so x²=50. Since sinC=√7/4, area=(1/2)x(2x)sinC=50√7/4=25√7/2.

7. [Maximum mark: 14]

A large school has students from Year 6 to Year 12. A group of 80 students in Year 12 were randomly selected and surveyed to find out how many hours per week they each spend doing homework. Their results are represented by the following cumulative frequency graph.

[Cumulative frequency graph: horizontal axis “number of hours” from 2 to 24 and vertical axis “cumulative frequency” from 0 to 80; the curve includes the readings (7,4), (14,40), (15,60), (18,72), (21,76) and (24,80).]

(a) Find the median number of hours per week these Year 12 students spend doing homework. [2]

(b) Given that 10% of these Year 12 students spend more than k hours per week doing homework, find the value of k. [3]

This same information is represented by the following table.

[Table: hours h and frequency: 2<h≤7: 4; 7<h≤15: p; 15<h≤21: 16; 21<h≤24: q.]

(c) Find the value of p and the value of q. [4]

There are 320 students in Year 12 at this school.

(d) Estimate the number of Year 12 students that spend more than 15 hours each week doing homework. [3]

(e) (i) Explain why this sampling method might not provide an accurate representation of the amount of time all of the students in the school spend doing homework.
(ii) Suggest a more appropriate sampling method. [2]
questions.solution: (a) The 40th value gives 14 h. (b) 72 are below k, giving k=18. (c) p=60−4=56 and q=80−76=4. (d) 20/80×320=80. (e) Only Year 12 was sampled; use a stratified random sample across all year groups.

Consider the function f defined by f(x)=6+6cosx, for 0≤x≤4π. The following diagram shows the graph of y=f(x). The graph of f touches the x-axis at points A and B. The shaded region is enclosed by the graph of y=f(x) and the x-axis, between A and B.

[Graph: y=6+6cosx on 0≤x≤4π, touching the x-axis at A and B; the region between the two points and the x-axis is shaded.]

(a) Find the x-coordinates of A and B. [3]

(b) Show that the area of the shaded region is 12π. [5]

The right cone in the following diagram has a total surface area of 12π, equal to the shaded area in the previous diagram. The cone has a base radius of 2, height h, and slant height l.

[Diagram not to scale: a right cone of base radius 2, height h and slant height l.]

(c) Find the value of l. [3]

(d) Hence, find the volume of the cone. [4]

9. [Maximum mark: 14]

Particle A travels in a straight line such that its displacement, s metres, from a fixed origin after t seconds is given by s(t)=8t−t², for 0≤t≤10, as shown in the following diagram.

[Displacement–time graph: the downward-opening parabola s=8t−t² on 0≤t≤10.]

Particle A starts at the origin and passes through the origin again when t=p.

(a) Find the value of p. [2]

Particle A changes direction when t=q.

(b) (i) Find the value of q.
(ii) Find the displacement of particle A from the origin when t=q. [4]

(c) Find the distance of particle A from the origin when t=10. [2]

The total distance travelled by particle A is given by d.

(d) Find the value of d. [2]

A second particle, particle B, travels along the same straight line such that its velocity is given by v(t)=14−2t, for t≥0. When t=k, the distance travelled by particle B is equal to d.

(e) Find the value of k. [4]
questions.solution: (a) t(8−t)=0 gives p=8. (b) v_A=8−2t=0 gives q=4 and s(4)=16. (c) s(10)=−20, distance 20. (d) 16 forward then 36 backward gives d=52. (e) B turns at 7; distance to k>7 is 49+(k−7)²=52, so k=7+√3.
